channel.title: Ghent Screens
channel.description: Daily screenings at Ghent's arthouse cinemas and film clubs, rarest films first, with who paid for each film. Kinepolis not included.

item.title: Ghent screens · Saturday 17 October · 20 films
item.description:
1. La Grande rêvasion (2× this week): Sphinx 11:00
    Funding: A 45-minute animation made for television by Autour de Minuit and Kwassa Films, co-produced by Canal+. It won the Annecy Cristal for TV production.
  2. The Pout-Pout Fish (2× this week): Sphinx 11:00
    Funding: An independently financed animation made for under $10 million by MIMO Studios, Like a Photon Creative, Cosmic Dino Studio, Alceon Entertainment and Eclectik Vision.
  3. Born in the Jungle (2× this week): Studio Skoop 14:30
    Funding: A Latvian-Polish-Czech animation by Atom Art, Letko and Hausboot. Shown as Magische Jungle at Studio Skoop. Sources we found name no funders.
  4. The Odyssey (2× this week): Studio Skoop 16:30
    Funding: Universal Pictures financed and distributes it, produced with Nolan and Emma Thomas's company Syncopy. At about $250 million it is one of Nolan's most expensive films. Studio Skoop shows it on 35mm.
  5. Trainspotting (1996) (2× this week): Studio Skoop 22:15
    Funding: Paid for by Channel Four Films, the film arm of the UK public-service broadcaster, and produced by Figment Films. PolyGram released it.
  6. Yugly (3× this week): Sphinx 14:30
    Funding: Brussels animation studio nWave made it with Octopolis. The Belgian tax shelter, raised through Umedia, and screen.brussels helped pay for it. Shown as Mochy in French.
  7. Garance (3× this week): Sphinx 17:30
    Funding: Produced in France by Chi-Fou-Mi Productions and Trésor Films, with Belgium's Artémis Productions as the foreign partner. StudioCanal distributes it in France and sells it internationally.
  8. Mémoire de fille (4× this week): Studio Skoop 17:00
    Funding: Judith Godrèche's adaptation of Annie Ernaux is produced by Windy Production. Paradise City Sales handles international sales and Jour2Fête releases it in France.
  9. L'Espèce explosive (4× this week): Sphinx 17:30
    Funding: A debut feature produced by 5à7 Films and built on public money. The Grand Est region backed it first, and France's CNC gave writing aid, an advance on receipts, music aid and distribution aid. The director says the CNC advance, won on the third try, unlocked the rest of the financing.
  10. The Last One for the Road (4× this week): Sphinx 17:30
    Funding: Original title Le città di pianura. Vivo Film produced it with Germany's Maze Pictures and Rai Cinema, the film arm of Italy's public broadcaster. Italy's culture ministry and the Council of Europe fund Eurimages also contributed.
  11. The Devils (1971) (4× this week): Studio Skoop 22:15
    Funding: Warner Bros. financed Ken Russell's film through Russo Productions and then cut it heavily for release. The new 4K restoration brings back material the studio removed.
  12. Notre salut (5× this week): Sphinx 14:00
    Funding: A Franco-Belgian co-production by Kidam and Brussels-based Michigan Films, made for under €5 million. Co-producers include France 2 Cinéma, Belgium's public broadcaster RTBF and Be tv/Proximus, and the CNC gave an advance on receipts plus development and distribution aid.
  13. Franz (7× this week): Studio Skoop 14:15 · 19:45
    Funding: A Kafka biopic stitched together from many public sources. Marlene Film (Prague), X Filme (Berlin) and Metro Films (Warsaw) produced it, joined by Czech, Polish and German broadcasters and Canal+. Funding came from Eurimages, the Czech Audiovisual Fund, the Polish Film Institute, Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg and Germany's DFFF.
  14. Sense and Sensibility (8× this week): Sphinx 11:00 · 20:15; Studio Skoop 17:00
    Funding: Working Title Films produced it with November Pictures and Kiddo Films. Working Title belongs to Universal, which releases the film internationally while its arthouse label Focus Features handles the US.
  15. The Social Reckoning (8× this week): Sphinx 11:00; Studio Skoop 22:15
    Funding: Made by Sony's Columbia Pictures with Alcon Entertainment and released worldwide by Sony Pictures. The reported budget is $30–42 million, modest for a studio film with this cast.
  16. Naza (8× this week): Sphinx 14:30 · 20:30; Studio Skoop 17:30
    Funding: A documentary from the No Other Land team, produced by James Wilson's JW Films with The Guardian, in association with Placeholder Films and Unseen Hand. Jonathan Glazer is an executive producer and mk2 Films handles world sales.
  17. Digger (10× this week): Studio Skoop 14:15 · 19:45; Sphinx 20:15
    Funding: A Hollywood studio picture: Legendary Pictures produced it in partnership with Warner Bros., which also distributes it. Tom Cruise is a producer alongside Iñárritu and Mary Parent. Warner Bros. says the budget stayed at $125 million; reports of $160–180 million were denied by the studio.
  18. Tegenwoordig heet iedereen sorry (10× this week): Studio Skoop 14:30; Sphinx 14:30
    Funding: A Flemish youth film produced by Ivy Vanhaecke at deMENSEN, with Germany's CALA Filmproduktion and Juliet at Pupkin. LevelK sells it abroad. The listing we found names no public funds.
  19. Primetime (10× this week): Sphinx 17:30; Studio Skoop 20:00
    Funding: A24 both finances and distributes this one. Robert Pattinson produces through his company Icki Eneo Arlo, with Range Media Partners and Square Peg also credited. No budget has been published.
  20. The Invite (14× this week): Sphinx 11:00 · 20:30; Studio Skoop 20:00 · 22:15
    Funding: Produced by Megan Ellison's Annapurna, then sold at Sundance 2026. A24 won a days-long bidding war against Focus Features and paid more than $12 million for the rights.
